parts.text: Data centers require enormous investments: land, buildings, computer equipment and power infrastructure. Yet, once they’re up and

, they tend to employ no more than a few dozen people in occupations such as IT technicians, engineers and security guards. With billions of dollars flowing into new data centers across the United States, communities are asking what they will get in return.

Skepticism about the
benefits of data centers is contributing to growing opposition to their construction, from Ohio to Texas. That pushback contributed to delays or cancellations of US$156 billion in

data center projects in 2025 alone.

We are professors who study real estate and urban economics, including how large place-based investments shape local economies. So we set out to answer a question at the center of these fights: Do data centers actually create jobs where they are built?

To find out, we teamed up with four
to study what happens to local employment after data centers open. We found that new data centers that opened from 2000-2023 created 1,000 to 1,300 jobs in the

where they are located, on average. But those jobs, which are for work performed outside data centers rather than inside them, take a few years to appear. They are mostly in industries that support data centers, not in restaurants or

.

How data centers create local jobs

Data centers can create jobs in at least three ways beyond employing people who work inside them.

First, they can increase demand for local suppliers, from security companies that protect the facilities to

contractors that maintain their equipment.

Second, data center employees and workers at these suppliers may spend more money locally, supporting restaurants, stores and other local services.

Third, companies already operating data centers may

their facilities, while other operators may decide to build nearby. Once a location has the electricity, fiber connections and other infrastructure needed to operate a data center, further investment may become easier.

Tracking data centers and jobs

We

detailed information on 1,584 U.S. data centers that opened between 2000 and 2023. For each facility, we recorded its location, opening date and power capacity, which is a standard way to compare facilities of different sizes. We then
these records with federal data on employment, wages and the number of businesses in each county.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

options: Data-centre development is associated with modest local employment growth rather than a jobs boom.
Resilience beyond short household emergencies depends on stronger food supply chains.
